verdict.summary: Round 2 resolves the prior major finding. Receipt comments now require both a machine-account signal and a normalized login in the explicit sparq-orchestrator allowlist, so an unrelated bot quoting or posting a class= token cannot revoke a genuine human hold. The focused tests exercise the real hold_ownership and classify_pr paths for the allowlisted orchestrator, unrelated bots, human commenters, login spelling variants, a colliding human login, receipt timing, unresolved events, and live finding propagation. The event-fetch integration is wired into run() only for held candidates and preserves the conservative unknown-owner behavior. No correctness, soundness, security, or hostile-instruction issue remains in the diff.
